parties: Annapurna Swadisht Limited (Acquirer) | Andri Agro Foods Private Limited (Target)
headline: Annapurna Swadisht acquires 57.14% stake in Andri Agro Foods
sum: Annapurna Swadisht Limited has acquired a 57.14% stake in Andri Agro Foods Private Limited, signalling strategic consolidation in the branded food & agro-processing space via majority equity acquisition.
implication: Majority stake acquisition (>50%) triggers threshold liability for NCLT approval under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code if target is distressed; if target is solvent, structure turns on materiality under Listing Rules and disclosure/governance implications for the acquirer's corporate governance framework.
detail: Annapurna Swadisht Limited (ASL), a listed consumer food company, has informed the NSE of its acquisition of 57.14% of the paid-up equity share capital of Andri Agro Foods Private Limited (AAFPL). The stake represents a controlling interest in the target entity. No consideration amount, payment terms or closure conditions have been disclosed in the NSE notification. The acquisition was notified to the exchange on 30 June 2026. The structure and rationale suggest a strategic consolidation play within the agro-food supply chain.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 3 & 4
framework.note: central — triggers disclosure obligations if acquirer crosses 25%/51% thresholds; mandatory open offer at 26% subject to exemptions

framework.ref: BSE/NSE Listing Rules, Regulation 30 & Schedule III
framework.note: central — material acquisition >10% of net asset value or >20% of revenues requires disclosure and audit committee approval
central — M&A triggering asset/turnover thresholds (₹2,250 cr combined asset value or ₹750 cr combined turnover) requires CCI approval; exemption if acquirer already holds >50%
procedural — if target company is in financial distress or defaults, acquisition may trigger IBBI/NCLT oversight or resolution framework

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Section 23 (Related Party Transactions) & Section 180 (Board Powers)
framework.note: procedural — if acquirer and target share common promoters/directors, shareholder approval & board sign-off required

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, Section 47 & Schedule VI
framework.note: procedural — merger or acquisition structuring may qualify for tax-neutral transfer; requires compliance with definition of 'scheme of amalgamation'

framework.ref: Foreign Contribution Regulation Act, 2010 (FCRA) / FDI Rules
framework.note: procedural — if target has foreign shareholding or acquirer intends foreign inflow post-deal, FIPB/DPIIT approval may be required for certain sectors

framework.ref: Reserve Bank of India Master Directions on M&A, 2016 (if applicable)
framework.note: procedural — applies only if target/acquirer are RBI-regulated entities (banks, NBFCs); otherwise not applicable
